rationale: All three lenses ran against the full 3-file/+90 diff and a complete acceptance criteria set; every AC and derived spec requirement passes, verified against source rather than the diff alone (the acceptance lens loaded the real shipped customer-config.yaml and confirmed get_enabled_components() emits exactly one allowedImageDomains item as {'enabled': True, 'availableForExternal': True, 'value': ''}, and confirmed by grep that no availableForExternal or auth filtering exists anywhere in src/). One blocking finding remains: CR-001, the new default-value test is the only test in its class that builds CustomerConfig() against the real, env-overridable CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR and asserts on the raw components list instead of get_enabled_components(), so it is both environment-fragile and does not actually prove the shipped default reaches the endpoint. 3 findings deferred as pre-existing, out of this change's scope: (a) ComponentSetting.value carries no type validation, so a YAML list or int reaches the UI untyped — same for bannerMessage and mcpAuthTimeoutSeconds today; (b) GET /v1/config is unauthenticated, so any operator-chosen hostnames in the list are readable anonymously — pre-existing endpoint posture that AC4 explicitly requires be broad; (c) the loader does not reject duplicate component ids. 8 findings dismissed: hostname validation/normalization (*, .com, whitespace, IDN, scheme/port stripping), the naive-suffix apex-matching ambiguity and the -only scope versus srcset/CSS/SVG vectors are all explicitly UI-side and out of scope per the ticket; the raw.githubusercontent.com example is the ticket's own canonical example, mirrored from codemie-ui!1616.

findings.title: Default-value test is environment-dependent and asserts the wrong layer
findings.problem: test_allowed_image_domains_default_is_empty is the only test in TestCustomerConfig that constructs CustomerConfig() without patching Path.read_text, so it reads whatever config.CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR resolves to. Config is a pydantic BaseSettings (src/codemie/configs/config.py), so CUSTOMER_CONFIG_DIR is overridable by an environment variable, and the default itself is Path(__file__).parents[3]/config/customer, which does not exist in an installed-package layout. It then asserts on config.components — the raw parse result — instead of get_enabled_components(), which is the list the endpoint actually serves.
findings.impact: The test's outcome depends on the environment rather than on the shipped config, so it can pass or fail for reasons unrelated to the change. More importantly it does not prove what AC3 requires: that the shipped default reaches GET /v1/config as an empty value. A regression that dropped the item from get_enabled_components() — for example someone adding allowedImageDomains to CONFIG_IDS — would leave this test green.
findings.recommendation: Pin the config path explicitly to the repo's shipped file, derived from the test file location rather than CWD or env (config_path=Path(__file__).resolve().parents[3] / "config/customer/customer-config.yaml"), and assert through get_enabled_components() instead of .components so the test covers the path the endpoint serves.
